title: Terraform module for VPC observability stack: Prometheus, Grafana, OpenTelemetry, and log shipping
creator: Maya Chen
description: Build a reusable Terraform module to deploy a hardened observability stack inside customer VPCs for Redwood Private deployments. The module will manage Prometheus (scraping + Alertmanager), Grafana (provisioned dashboards + datasource), OpenTelemetry Collector (receiving/exporting traces/metrics), and log forwarding (Fluent Bit) with pluggable destinations. The goal is a single, well-documented IaC artifact that operators can enable during Private/VPC installs and that supports upgrades, health checks, and minimal blast radius by default.
acceptance_criteria: Terraform module with inputs/outputs documented in README.md
Deploys Prometheus + Alertmanager via Helm with service monitors for runtime components
Grafana is provisioned with 5 prebuilt dashboards (runtime metrics, latency, token cost, model usage, node health) and a configured datasource pointing to Prometheus

OpenTelemetry Collector deployed as a highly available statefulset/daemonset (configurable) and able to export to at least two backends (OTLP receiver -> customer endpoint / S3/OTel-compatible backend)
Fluent Bit deployed and able to forward logs to configurable destinations (S3, OpenSearch, or HTTP endpoint) and supports Kubernetes metadata enrichment

Automated post-deploy health checks verify: all pods Ready, Prometheus scrape endpoint returns 200 for /metrics, OTel collector accepts a test trace, and a sample log appears in destination within 5 minutes
Module supports safe upgrades (helm upgrade with readiness checks) and exposes variables to control upgrade strategy
Module terraform plan/apply can run in a customer VPC without exposing control plane endpoints publicly
E2E Terratest (or equivalent) located in infra/test validates deploy -> scrape -> trace -> log flow in CI
implementation_notes: Design module to be cloud-agnostic but with opinionated AWS defaults (EKS integration, Security Groups, IAM roles for service accounts)
Expose Helm chart values as module-level inputs rather than embedding complex YAML in Terraform
Use Helm provider with dependency on kubernetes provider; prefer provider 'helm' v2+ features for wait and atomic upgrades
Create optional toggles: enable_grafana=false, enable_prometheus=true, otel_mode="daemonset"|"deployment", log_forwarder="fluentbit"|"none"
Provide output variables: grafana_url (private), prometheus_endpoint, otel_collector_endpoint, log_forwarder_service
Implement Kubernetes null_resource provisioner steps for post-deploy verification using kubectl/otel-cli/awslocal where needed
Include terraform testing via Terratest and unit tests for Terraform modules using terraform-compliance where feasible
Add module acceptance tests in CI gated by flag (infra-observability-e2e) to avoid noisy runs for every PR
upgrade_strategy: Default Helm upgrade with --wait and timeout; set maxUnavailable for deployments to 1 to reduce blast radius
Support canary release mode by allowing namespace-scoped, temp-label-based Helm release and swap; documented as opt-in advanced workflow
Provide a 'pre_upgrade_hook' and 'post_upgrade_hook' null_resource script path so customers can run validation scripts
Keep backward-compatible default values for collector/prometheus so minor upgrades don't require forced replacement
Document manual rollback steps and automatic alerting rules that fire if >25% of pods fail readiness during upgrade
health_checks: Kubernetes readiness/liveness probes configured for all components
Terraform null_resource runs: kubectl get pods --namespace ${var.namespace} --selector app in (prometheus, grafana, otel-collector, fluent-bit) and verifies Ready count == desired
Grafana health endpoint /api/health returns 200 and admin user can authenticate with provided creds
OTel Collector accepts a synthetic OTLP trace via otel-cli or curl and exporter confirms send to destination
Log flow test: inject test log into a pod and confirm ingestion to configured destination within 5 minutes
Expose optional CloudWatch/Cloud Monitoring alarms for key metrics (scrape_errors_total, collector_received_spans, fluentbit_output_errors)
migration_plan: Phase 1: Implement module and deploy to internal staging VPC; validate metrics/logs/traces end-to-end
Phase 2: Provide migration scripts to copy Grafana dashboards and Prometheus rules from legacy deployment (if present)
Phase 3: Offer one-click switch for customer installs: enable module and shift DNS endpoints (private) to new services
Phase 4: Run parallel observers for 24-72 hours, compare metrics and costs, then decommission legacy collectors
risks: Collector misconfiguration could cause PII to be forwarded to incorrect destinations; security review required
Resource overhead (CPU/memory) for Prometheus in large clusters; we may need remote_write or Thanos/long-term storage option
Network policy and VPC egress rules may block exporters; module must include clear SG/NACL guidance
Upgrade-induced downtime if Helm charts change retention/volume claims; need migration docs for persistent volumes
Log shipping to customer-owned sinks may vary widely (S3, OpenSearch, Splunk); support matrix required
qa_checks: Run terraform plan and apply in isolated staging VPC using module defaults
Execute Terratest suite validating Prometheus scrape, Grafana auth, OTel trace path, and log ingestion
Simulate upgrade path from previous minor version and verify no data loss for metrics >1 hour window
Run security scan on Helm charts and collector config for sensitive exporter configs
Verify that destroyed resources do not leave PVs or IAM roles behind
